title: Exercise May Ease 'Chemo Brain'
hook: Up to 80% of chemotherapy patients get foggy thinking. In a new trial, a home-based exercise program improved attention and reduced noticeable cognitive problems compared with a placebo.
key_points: 'Chemo brain' — trouble with focus and memory — affects up to 80% of people on chemotherapy.
In a trial, patients doing a home-based exercise program had better attention than those on placebo.
They also reported fewer noticeable cognitive problems in everyday tasks.
Low-dose ibuprofen improved some measures too, but its effects were less consistent.
content_html: "Chemo brain" — the fuzzy thinking, slow recall, and trouble focusing that can come with chemotherapy — is common, affecting up to 80% of patients. A new trial points to a simple, accessible counter: a home-based exercise program left patients with sharper attention and fewer everyday cognitive complaints than a placebo.
extra_html: Researchers also tested low-dose ibuprofen, which improved some cognitive measures, though the effects were less consistent than exercise's. The program was home-based, meaning patients didn't need a gym or supervision. As always, anyone in cancer treatment should clear a new exercise routine with their care team first. Reported by ScienceDaily.

related.title: How Much Exercise You Actually Need
related.hook: The headline number is smaller than most people fear: about 150 minutes of moderate activity a week — roughly 20-some minutes a day — moves the needle on your health.

related.title: Keeping Your Brain Healthy
related.hook: No pill prevents dementia, but the habits that protect your heart turn out to protect your brain too.
